messages:
devraj: Hey support — our /v1/rerank calls started returning a 410 with "model_deprecated" after a deploy last night. Example call we sent:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-default-v0","query":"how to reset password","documents":["doc1","doc2"]}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 410 Gone` + body: `{"error":{"code":410,"message":"model redwood/rerank-default-v0 is deprecated"}}`
Anyone seeing this?

elaine_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the full response body & the request_id from the response headers if you have it? Also which tenant/org is this from?

devraj: Sure — request_id header: `req_8b3f2`
Full response body:
```json
{"error":{"code":410,"message":"model redwood/rerank-default-v0 is deprecated","suggested_replacement":"redwood/rerank-v1"}}
```
Tenant: acme-analytics-prod

elaine_support: Thanks — that suggests the alias `redwood/rerank-default-v0` was deprecated and we have a replacement. Could you try calling with `redwood/rerank-v1` and see if that succeeds? Also, sometimes clients cache aliases; clearing any local model-id cache helps.

devraj: Tried `redwood/rerank-v1` — request returns 200 but the scores are all 0.0 (looks wrong):
```json
{"results":[{"id":0,"score":0.0},{"id":1,"score":0.0}],"request_id":"req_8b41a"}
```
We didn't change payload other than model id.

samir_eng_ml: Quick thought — scores of exactly 0.0 usually mean the model accepted the request but ranked effectively-equal inputs (or we hit a preprocessing issue that resulted in empty embeddings). Can you paste the exact request body you sent to v1? Also include content-length / encoding if possible.

devraj: Here's the body we sent (exact):
```json
{"model":"redwood/rerank-v1","query":"how to reset password","documents":"[\"doc1\", \"doc2\"]"}
```
…ah, looking at this now I see `documents` is a stringified array (we're serializing twice in our SDK wrapper). Oops.

samir_eng_ml: That would explain it — the renker receives `documents` as a single string, then tokenization/embedding path yields degenerate vectors -> near-zero similarity -> zero scores. If you send `documents` as a proper JSON array it should return meaningful scores.

ingrid_sre: FWIW, on infra side we saw a few hits to the alias-mapping service returning redirects to archived ids during the deploy window. Some clients with sticky caches hit the old alias and then used the replacement id (good) but a couple of edge cases caused mismatched preprocessing (like the double-serialized payload). We're clearing stale alias cache entries for the tenant and adding a short TTL to mitigate this.

devraj: Replayed with fixed payload (documents as array) and pinned `redwood/rerank-v1` in our config — now getting sensible scores:
```json
{"results":[{"id":0,"score":0.92},{"id":1,"score":0.14}],"request_id":"req_8b4f0"}
```
Thanks — that fixes it.

elaine_support: Great to hear! I'll mark this thread resolved. Two quick recommendations: 1) pin model ids in prod (aliases can change), 2) add a client-side validation that `documents` is an array and warn on string input. Would you like us to open an SRE ticket to enable a tenant-scoped alias redirect for `redwood/rerank-default-v0` -> `redwood/rerank-v1` to avoid this for other clients?

devraj: Yes please, that would help during our rollout. Also please add a short note on the SDK docs about not double-serializing. :thumbsup:

elaine_support: Roger — opening ticket now (SRE-6821). I'll follow up via email with the ETA. Thanks for the clear repro and quick follow-up.

deploy-bot: Deployment job redwood/alias-service #472 completed — rolling back stale cache entries for tenant acme-analytics-prod

ingrid_sre: Confirmed cleanup started; we pushed a TTL change and invalidated the tenant cache. Will close SRE-6821 after monitoring period.

devraj: Confirmed all good on our side. Appreciate the fast help! :heart:
